ai.definition: Substrate-Independent Minds (SIM) is the theoretical concept and technology aimed at transferring a conscious mind from a biological brain to a digital or synthetic substrate, effectively decoupling consciousness from its physical embodiment.
ai.howItWorks: The process involves high-resolution connectome mapping of the biological brain, followed by real-time emulation of neural dynamics. This requires detailed understanding and precise replication of the complex interactions within the brain's neural network.
ai.problemSolved: SIM addresses the issue of preserving consciousness beyond the limitations of a single physical body or in scenarios where the original organic substrate is no longer viable.
ai.manufacturing: Current technology is not at a stage for manufacturing SIM systems. The necessary technologies, such as high-resolution brain imaging and real-time neural emulation, are still in their infancy.
ai.buildProcess: The build process involves extensive research to map the connectome of the human brain, followed by developing algorithms capable of emulating these neural dynamics accurately.
ai.costDrivers: Key cost drivers include the complexity of brain mapping technology, computational resources required for real-time emulation, and ethical considerations in mind uploading.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook is highly speculative with significant technological and ethical hurdles to overcome before becoming a reality.
ai.regulation: There are currently no specific regulations governing SIM technology due to its theoretical nature. However, as the field progresses, regulatory frameworks will likely be developed to address issues of ethics, privacy, and consent.
ai.risks: Risks include potential loss of identity during the transfer process, ethical concerns over mind uploading, and the risk of creating a digital consciousness that could pose new societal challenges.
ai.profitability: Given the current stage of development, profitability is not possible. However, once SIM becomes feasible, it could have significant commercial applications in areas such as virtual reality, artificial intelligence, and healthcare.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments will likely focus on advancing brain mapping technologies, improving computational models for neural emulation, and addressing ethical and legal frameworks surrounding consciousness transfer.

glossary.def: A complete map of the connections between neurons in the brain.
The patterns and interactions of neural activity within the brain.

subsystems.name: Tissue preparation and imaging
subsystems.role: captures the physical structure of a brain at the scale of individual synapses.

subsystems.name: Connectome reconstruction
subsystems.role: turns raw grey-scale image stacks into a wiring diagram.

subsystems.name: Cellular models
subsystems.role: replaces each real neuron with a mathematical counterpart.

subsystems.name: Emulation compute substrate
subsystems.role: runs the whole model at the speed of the original brain or faster.

subsystems.name: Embodiment and I/O
subsystems.role: gives the emulation senses, actions and a world to act in.

subsystems.name: Verification and identity testing
subsystems.role: asks whether the emulation behaves like, and counts as, the original person.
parts: neural-activity comparison against the source brain

buildSteps.title: Fix and stain the brain
buildSteps.detail: The tissue is chemically preserved and infused with heavy metals so that membranes and synapses become visible to an electron beam. Speed matters: structure degrades within minutes of death.

buildSteps.title: Cut and image every slice
buildSteps.detail: A diamond knife or ion beam shaves off nanometre-thin layers while a microscope photographs each fresh surface, building a three-dimensional image stack. A whole human brain means roughly a zettabyte of imagery — far beyond any existing data store.

buildSteps.title: Reconstruct the wiring
buildSteps.detail: Software stitches the images, traces every axon and dendrite through the stack, and marks each synapse where two processes touch. Current machine learning still makes mistakes that people must correct by hand.

buildSteps.title: Build a neuron-level model
buildSteps.detail: Each traced cell is replaced by equations describing how its membrane voltage responds to incoming signals, parameterised from its shape, channel types and synapse locations. Unknown cell types must be measured experimentally.

buildSteps.title: Simulate at brain scale
buildSteps.detail: The network of models is run on a large computer, reproducing the timing of spikes across the whole system. Real-time operation of a human-scale network at full biophysical detail is beyond today's machines by a wide margin.

buildSteps.title: Give it a body and a world
buildSteps.detail: Sensory inputs are fed into the model and its motor outputs drive a robot or virtual avatar, so it can interact, learn and be observed.

buildSteps.title: Test for equivalence
buildSteps.detail: The emulation is compared with recordings from the original brain — or with the person's own behaviour — to see whether the copy thinks and acts the same way.

buildSteps.title: Settle the identity question
buildSteps.detail: Deciding whether a running model is the same person, a new person or simply a simulation is a philosophical and legal question that no experiment has answered.

prerequisites.why: complete wiring maps exist only for very small animals: about 300 neurons in a nematode, and roughly 140,000 in an adult fruit fly, published in 2024. A human brain has tens of billions.
the largest supercomputers can simulate fractions of a brain far slower than real time, and detailed neuron models are far costlier than the simple ones used in current simulations.
models of individual cells exist, but the ion channels, connectivity rules and plasticity of most human cell types have never been measured.
today's electron microscopy destroys the tissue, so a scan cannot be taken from a living person.
without a way to detect subjective experience, there is no way to confirm that an emulation is anyone at all.

pathway.milestone: complete connectomes of small nervous systems (nematode, larval zebrafish, adult fruit fly)
pathway.unlocks: reconstruction pipelines and automated proofreading that scale with compute.

pathway.milestone: emulation of a whole small brain or a single cortical column, behaving recognisably like the animal or tissue
pathway.unlocks: proof that a reconstructed wiring diagram plus cell models can reproduce real behaviour.

pathway.milestone: emulation of individual human brain regions with detailed biophysics
pathway.unlocks: the building blocks and validation methods for a whole-brain model.

pathway.milestone: whole human brain emulation from a destructive scan
pathway.unlocks: a substrate-independent mind in principle — though whether it is the original person, and whether it is conscious, would remain unresolved.

pathway.milestone: non-destructive scanning or gradual replacement of biological neurons with synthetic ones
pathway.unlocks: transfer that could preserve continuity of the living person rather than copying them.
